tasks.title: Rework list into two-line default with --oneline and active marker
tasks.description:
**Context** — First lap of the `improve-cli-ergonomics` change (branch from current `main`; it is the prerequisite for the other three changes in the chain). Source of truth: `openspec/changes/improve-cli-ergonomics/` — `design.md` (Decisions: two-line layout, --oneline, claim-reader marker), `specs/task-listing/spec.md` (SHALLs + scenarios), `tasks.md` §1 (1.1–1.4, 1.8). Today `internal/cmd/list.go` renders one line per lap via `formatListTask` (`<n>. <id> — <title>` plus ` (assignee: <a>)` only when the assignee is non-empty). Existing list assertions in `internal/cmd/cmd_test.go` — `TestListDefault`, `TestListOutputUnchangedWithoutAssignee`, `TestListOutputIncludesAssignee`, and the `Contains(out, id+" — ...")` / `idxBefore(..., "— A", "— B")` ordering checks — assert that one-line shape and WILL break.

**Outcome** — `laps list` defaults to two lines per lap; `--oneline` reproduces the prior single-line shape byte-for-byte; done laps strike correctly in both modes; the active (claimed) lap shows `> ` and only that lap; the existing test suite compiles and passes with migrated assertions.

**Files & scope** — `internal/cmd/list.go` (add a `listOneline` bool flag in `init`; add a two-line formatter; KEEP `formatListTask` verbatim and route `--oneline` through it; call `store.ReadClaim(beadsDir)` once to resolve the active id). `internal/cmd/cmd_test.go` (migrate the list assertions per 1.8 — re-point the terse-shape ones at `--oneline` so the legacy format stays under test rather than getting deleted). Do NOT add the `ls` alias or touch `hooks.go` here (later lap). Do NOT write the full new test matrix (later lap) — only the migration needed to keep the suite green.

**Design** — Per design.md "Two-line layout": line 1 = `<n>. [> ]<title>` (marker `> ` prefix on the title when this lap is the active one; title wrapped in `~~` when done); line 2 = `<indent><id> · <assignee|—> · <todo|done>` where the assignee placeholder is an em dash when unset and `<indent>` is padded to the width of the line-1 position prefix `"<n>. "` so the id column stays aligned past 9 laps (a fixed 3-space indent misaligns at position 10+). `--oneline` MUST reuse today's `formatListTask` verbatim — the ` (assignee: <a>)` clause is appended ONLY when the assignee is non-empty (this is what `TestListOutputUnchangedWithoutAssignee` locks in; do not make the clause unconditional). Done styling: two-line mode strikes only the title; `--oneline` preserves the prior whole-line `~~...~~` strike. Active marker: call the central claim-reader `store.ReadClaim(beadsDir)` (already used by `claim`/`done`); do NOT read `.laps/claim` directly in the formatter. Missing claim file → no marker (ReadClaim returns "" on not-exist). Claim id not present in the rendered result → no marker. A claim-read error other than not-exist must fail the command via the normal error path. This is the change's only user-visible behavior change and the highest-risk lap — the default output is the most-consumed contract — so a VERIFY lap follows immediately.

**Acceptance** — `just build` and `just test` green. `bin/laps add tail --title A && bin/laps add tail --title B && bin/laps list` prints four lines (two per lap) with id/assignee/state on line 2 and no descriptions. `bin/laps list --oneline` prints the prior single-line shape. `bin/laps list --all` after a `done` strikes the title (two-line) or the whole line (--oneline). Migrated assertions pass and the legacy format stays under test via `--oneline`. Smoke: with `bin/laps claim` active, the claimed lap shows `> ` and others do not; with no claim, no marker.

tasks.title: Add ls alias and list rendering tests
tasks.description:
**Context** — Follows the verified two-line formatter. Implements tasks 1.5, 1.6, and the full new test matrix 1.7. `internal/cmd/hooks.go:isKnownCommand` (around line 102) gates the hook-only intercept: names not in that list are treated as hook-only commands and never reach built-in dispatch, so `ls` must be recognized as a built-in.

**Outcome** — `laps ls` works identically to `laps list` (same flags, same output) and dispatches as a built-in; the list formatter is covered by focused tests for the two-line default, `--oneline`, the three marker states, the `ls` alias, and `--json-output`.

**Files & scope** — `internal/cmd/list.go` (register `ls` as an alias of `listCmd` via cobra's `Aliases` field — flags flow through automatically). `internal/cmd/hooks.go` (add `"ls"` to the `isKnownCommand` switch). `internal/cmd/cmd_test.go` (add the 1.7 test matrix).

**Design** — The alias is mechanical: set `listCmd.Aliases = []string{"ls"}` and cobra reuses `listCmd`'s flag set and Run. The `isKnownCommand` addition MUST land with the alias or `ls` would be misrouted to the hook-only intercept. For the marker tests, reuse the claim setup pattern from `TestDoneWithClaim` (setupTempRepo + `runMB("claim")`) and cover the three spec scenarios: claimed lap is the only one marked (exactly one `> `); no claim → no marker; a claim for an id outside the rendered result → no marker (e.g., claim a done lap then `list` without `--all`, or claim then delete). Assert `--json-output` is unchanged in structure (still `{"tasks":[...]}`). Assert `--oneline` matches the legacy `<n>. <id> — <title>` shape. Cover `ls` dispatch through `runMBExecute` (the real argv path) so the alias plus hook recognition is exercised end-to-end.

**Acceptance** — `just test` green with the new tests; `bin/laps ls` and `bin/laps ls --oneline` match `bin/laps list` and `bin/laps list --oneline` byte-for-byte; a hook config that would intercept an unknown command does NOT intercept `ls`.

tasks.title: Add move command reusing ComputeInsertOrder
tasks.description:
**Context** — Implements tasks 2.1–2.6 (tests 2.7 are a separate lap). `store.ComputeInsertOrder` (`internal/store/store.go:344`) already implements head/tail/after ordering with midpoint insertion and renumber-on-gap-exhaustion; it returns `(order, fallbackHead, err)` and `store.ErrTaskNotFound` for a missing `after` target. `add.go` (lines 155–166) is the reference for consuming it: call ComputeInsertOrder, map `ErrTaskNotFound` to exit 3, and when `fallbackHead` is true emit the stderr notice. Note ComputeInsertOrder only RETURNS `fallbackHead` — it does not print — so `move.go` must emit the after-done notice itself. `internal/cmd/hooks.go:isKnownCommand` must recognize `move`.

**Outcome** — `laps move <id> head|tail|after <id>` reorders an existing TODO lap, preserving its id, with exit codes mirroring `add`, hook lifecycle, JSON output, and `updatedAt` advancement.

**Files & scope** — New `internal/cmd/move.go` (one file per subcommand, per AGENTS.md; mirror `add.go`'s structure: package-level flag vars, a `moveCmd *cobra.Command`, an `init()` registering it). `internal/cmd/hooks.go` (add `"move"` to `isKnownCommand`). Do NOT add edit/assign here.

**Design** — Exit-code mirroring is the subtle part and must match design.md "Exit codes mirror add": an `after` target that does not exist → exit 3 via `store.ErrTaskNotFound` (as `add.go:157`); a moved id that is unknown or already done, and any usage error → exit 1; `move <id> after <id>` (self-reference) → error, do not silently no-op. Operate on TODO laps only — an already-done moved id errors (exit 1). On success: set the task's `Order` to the computed order, advance `UpdatedAt = time.Now().UTC()`, and preserve `ID`/`Title`/`Description`/`Assignee`/`IsDone`/`CreatedAt`/`CompletedAt` exactly, then `store.Save`. When `fallbackHead` is true, emit the after-done notice to stderr yourself, copying the `fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, …)` pattern from `add.go:164` (`laps: lap %s already complete; added to next available spot (head).\n`). Non-JSON success prints ONLY the affected lap id on stdout (warnings/notices to stderr). Honor `--json-output` with `{"task": <task>}` (single-object form, matching `add`'s non-batch JSON shape). Run before/after hooks with the affected task pointer set and `$output`/`$exit_code` populated, reusing the `runBeforeHooks` / `runAfterHooksDeferred` pattern from `add.go`. Arg parsing: `move <id> <position>` and `move <id> after <target>`.

**Acceptance** — `just build` and `just lint` green. Smoke: add three laps A,B,C; `move <C-id> head` then `list --oneline` shows C first; `move <A-id> after <C-id>`; the id is unchanged before/after (capture id, move, re-`get`). `move <done-id> head` exits 1 with a clear message; `move <id> after <missing>` exits 3; `move <id> after <done-id>` moves to head with the stderr notice; `move <id> after <id>` errors; `--json-output` returns the task object. The full test matrix is the next lap.

tasks.title: Add move command tests
tasks.description:
**Context** — Implements task 2.7. The `move` command (previous lap) reuses `store.ComputeInsertOrder` with `add`-style exit codes. Follow the existing test patterns in `internal/cmd/cmd_test.go` (`runMB` for in-process, `runMBExecute` for the real argv dispatch path).

**Outcome** — `move` is covered for every branch: positions, id preservation, error exits, after-done fallback, hook context, dispatch, and updatedAt.

**Files & scope** — `internal/cmd/cmd_test.go` only.

**Design** — One focused test per scenario family: move to head/tail/after and confirm resulting order via `list --oneline` + `idxBefore`; id is byte-identical before/after (capture id, move, re-get); done moved id → exit 1; unknown moved id → exit 1; missing `after` target → exit 3; after-done target → fallback to head AND the stderr notice is present (assert on stderr); `move <id> after <id>` self-reference → error; `--json-output` returns `{"task":...}` with the preserved id; `updatedAt` strictly advances (seed the task, capture UpdatedAt via `get --json-output` or `store.Load`, move, confirm advancement); a `runMBExecute("move", ...)` test so the built-in dispatch + `isKnownCommand` path is exercised. Add a move hook-context test mirroring the existing hook-context test pattern (before/after fire with the affected task's id/title in vars), if such a helper exists.

**Acceptance** — `just test` green; every exit-code branch has a dedicated assertion.

tasks.title: Add edit and assign commands
tasks.description:
**Context** — Implements tasks 3.1–3.7 (tests 3.8 and the harness reset 3.9 are a separate lap). The reference for `Changed`-gating is `add.go:73` (`flagMode := cmd.Flags().Changed("title") || ...`). `edit` and `assign` are new mutating built-ins; both must be added to `internal/cmd/hooks.go:isKnownCommand` before the hook-only intercept.

**Outcome** — `laps edit <id> [--title] [--description] [--assignee]` and `laps assign <id> <role>` update fields in place, bump `updatedAt`, honor `--json-output`, run hooks, and follow the done-lap warning rule.

**Files & scope** — New `internal/cmd/edit.go` and `internal/cmd/assign.go` (one file per subcommand). `internal/cmd/hooks.go` (add `"edit"` and `"assign"` to `isKnownCommand`). Do NOT extend the test reset harness here — that is the next lap — but note that the package-level flag vars you add (e.g. `editTitle`/`editDescription`/`editAssignee`) are exactly what that harness must zero.

**Design** — The crux (3.1): gate each field on `cmd.Flags().Changed("<name>")`, NOT on a non-empty value, so `--description ""` (clear) is distinguishable from an unset flag. Require ≥1 field via `Changed("title") || Changed("description") || Changed("assignee")`, else exit 1. This `Changed`-gating is subtle and is exactly why the test harness reset (next lap) is load-bearing — a leaked `Changed=true` between tests silently corrupts the next edit. Semantics (3.5): `--title` must be non-blank after trimming (else error); `--description ""` clears the description; `--assignee ""` clears the assignee; non-empty assignees are trimmed; escaped `\n` in descriptions follows `add` (`strings.ReplaceAll(desc, "\\n", "\n")`). Done-lap rule (3.6): `edit`/`assign` may target a done lap — succeed with a stderr warning, do NOT reopen it (keep `IsDone=true`, keep `completedAt`). `assign <id> <role>` is sugar for `edit <id> --assignee <role>`; a blank role clears the assignee (3.2, 3.5). Non-JSON success prints ONLY the affected id on stdout; warnings to stderr. `--json-output` → `{"task": <task>}`. Run before/after hooks with the affected task and `$output`/`$exit_code` (mirror add/move). Advance `UpdatedAt` on success. Unknown id → exit 1.

**Acceptance** — `just build` and `just lint` green. Smoke: `edit <id> --title "New"` updates title; `edit <id> --description ""` clears (verify via `get`); `edit <id> --assignee ""` clears; `edit <id>` with no flags errors; `assign <id> coder` sets assignee; `assign <id> ""` clears; editing a done lap warns on stderr and leaves it done; `--json-output` returns the task. The full test matrix + reset-harness extension is the next lap.

tasks.title: Add edit and assign tests and extend flag-reset harness
tasks.description:
**Context** — Implements tasks 3.8 (tests) and 3.9 (reset harness). This lap is load-bearing for the whole test suite's correctness because `edit`'s semantics hinge on `cmd.Flags().Changed`. The existing reset harness in `internal/cmd/cmd_test.go` — `runMB` (around line 33) and `runMBExecute` (around line 89) — zeroes package-level vars and resets `flag.Changed` via a `pflag.FlagSet` loop. That loop currently registers `rootCmd.PersistentFlags()`, `addCmd.Flags()`, `listCmd.Flags()`, `updateCmd.Flags()`, `doneUndoCmd.Flags()`.

**Outcome** — `edit`/`assign` are fully tested and the reset harness registers the new flagsets so no `Changed=true` leaks between tests.

**Files & scope** — `internal/cmd/cmd_test.go` only.

**Design** — 3.9 (critical): in BOTH `runMB` and `runMBExecute`, add `editCmd.Flags()`, `moveCmd.Flags()`, and `assignCmd.Flags()` to the `pflag.FlagSet` loop, and zero the new package-level vars (`listOneline`, the `edit*` vars, the `move*` vars) alongside the existing `addTitle`/`addDescription`/etc. The `list` flagset (already in the loop) covers `--oneline` automatically. Why this matters: a leaked `Changed=true` — e.g. a prior test's `--description ""` — makes a later title-only edit silently clear the description; a single missing registration corrupts unrelated tests. 3.8 tests: edit each field independently; no-flags → exit 1; field validation (blank title errors, `--description ""` clears, `--assignee ""` clears, non-empty assignee trims, escaped `\n` in description); blank `assign` clears assignee; done-target warns on stderr AND preserves `IsDone`/`completedAt`; `assign` sets assignee; non-JSON success prints only the id; `--json-output` returns `{"task":...}`; hook context fires with the affected task; a `runMBExecute("edit"/"assign", ...)` dispatch test.

**Acceptance** — `just test` green and stable across `go test -count=2 ./internal/cmd` (the repeat run confirms no `Changed`-leak flakiness). Every edit/assign branch asserted.

tasks.title: Update README command reference for new commands
tasks.description:
**Context** — Implements task 4.1 (docs). All new commands (`ls`, `move`, `edit`, `assign`) and the `list` two-line/`--oneline` behavior now exist and are verified. Task 4.2 is a non-action — do NOT bump `VERSION`; the 0.9.0 bump belongs to the `add-stints-gating` change.

**Outcome** — `README.md` command reference documents the new surface accurately and no longer lists these names as reserved hook-only command names.

**Files & scope** — `README.md` only. Do NOT touch `VERSION` (4.2). Do NOT touch `openspec/` or source.

**Design** — Mirror the existing README command-reference tone and format. Document: `list` two-line default + `--oneline` for the prior shape; `ls` as an alias of `list`; `move <id> head|tail|after <id>` (note the id is preserved); `edit <id> [--title] [--description] [--assignee]` (≥1 flag required; `""` clears a field); `assign <id> <role>`. If the README lists reserved/hook-only command names anywhere, remove `ls`/`move`/`edit`/`assign` from that list (they are now built-ins). Keep it scoped to user-visible behavior — no internal implementation detail.

**Acceptance** — README renders; commands and flags match the actual binary (`bin/laps list --help`, `bin/laps move --help`, `bin/laps edit --help`, `bin/laps assign --help`); the `VERSION` file is unchanged.
